act.name: Discover
act.tagline: What's really there — and can we build it?

title: Feasibility & the Technical Decision
goal: Choose one approach explicitly, with feasibility, effort and risk on the table, and record it so PLAN starts from evidence.

processes.title: Feasibility & the Technical Decision
processes.summary: Assess feasibility, estimate effort, risk and cost, compare the options and record the decision as an ADR for PLAN.

definition.purpose: Choose one approach explicitly, with feasibility, effort and risk on the table, and record it so PLAN starts from evidence.
definition.outcome: An accepted ADR, the estimates and risks behind it, and a handoff pack for PLAN.
definition.jtbd: When the options are proven, help me choose one, say what it costs and risks, and record why.

normal: Record the decision (ADR) → hand off to Plan

cases.happyPath: One option is feasible, affordable and clearly best.
alternates: Conditional decision → conditions dated in the ADR
Close call → choose the cheaper-to-reverse option
exceptions: Key unknown remains → one more spike first

routing.escalation: Risk or trade-off beyond the tech lead → client
routing.stop: Not feasible → ADR says 'do not build'; learning logged

checks: Tech lead sign-off on feasibility and the ADR
rules: Every outcome is recorded — including 'do not build'

decisions: Which approach do we build, and why?

execution.authority: Tech lead owns the technical decision; the client decides risks and trade-offs above that authority.

continuity.handoff: ADR & handoff pack → PLAN; learning log → EVOLVE
traceability: Creates EST-##, RSK-## and ADR-### linking TPS-##, ARO-## and SPK-##

lessons.title: Assess Technical Feasibility
lessons.summary: Rate each option's feasibility from the evidence: unknowns, quality risks, skills and conditions.

definition.purpose: Say, with evidence, whether each option can be built and run here — and on what conditions.
definition.outcome: A feasibility assessment per option: rating, unknowns and how they were resolved, quality attributes at risk, skills and conditions.
definition.jtbd: Help me know which options we can really build and run, and what must be true for that.
exit: Each option rated high / medium / low with evidence

normal: Gather spike results and remaining unknowns per option

cases.happyPath: One option is clearly feasible with few conditions.
alternates: Feasible only with a vendor commitment → make it a condition
edgeCases: Skills missing → rate with the training or hire it needs
exceptions: Remaining unknown is critical → one more spike first

routing.forward: Feasibility assessment → 1.5.2 Estimate Effort, Risk & Cost
routing.alternate: Clear single option → assess it and the fallback
routing.escalation: Condition outside the team's control → tech lead and client
routing.stop: Nothing feasible → stop and record why — recorded in the learning log

criteria: Every rating cites spike results or docs
rules: An unknown is never rated as low risk
policies: Feasibility signed off by the tech lead

decisions: Can we build and run it here?

agents: AI coding agent for challenging the ratings
execution.authority: Tech lead signs off the ratings.

continuity.handoff: Feasibility assessment → 1.5.2 Estimate Effort, Risk & Cost
traceability: Ratings link to SPK-## and ARO-##
measures: Unknowns that became problems in BUILD

workflows.title: Rate Feasibility
workflows.summary: Rate each architecture option's feasibility from the spike results and remaining unknowns, and write the conditions each rating depends on.

steps.title: Gather evidence & unknowns per option
steps.ask: For each architecture option, collect the spike results that support it and the unknowns that remain.

lenses.note: Spike results and what's still unknown.

steps.title: Rate each option
steps.ask: Rate each option's feasibility high / medium / low, citing the evidence, and name the quality attributes at risk.

steps.title: Write skills & conditions
steps.ask: List the skills and capacity each option needs versus what the team has, and write each rating's conditions as checkable, dated facts.

lenses.note: Who will run it, and do they have the skills?

steps.title: Feasible?
steps.ask: Prepare the feasibility call for the tech lead: which options are feasible, and on what conditions.

lenses.note: Is at least one option feasible, and on what conditions?

contract.definition: Rate each architecture option's feasibility from the spike results and remaining unknowns, and write the conditions each rating depends on.
decisions: Is at least one option feasible?
recovery: Rewrite conditions as dated, checkable facts
contract.handoff: Feasibility assessment → 1.5.2 Estimate Effort, Risk & Cost
traceability: Ratings link to SPK-## and ARO-##
learning: Unknowns that became problems later — learning log

lessons.exercise: Rate option A's feasibility and write two dated conditions. Then do the same for your own project.

quiz.q: An unknown hasn't been spiked. How do you rate it?
options: As a risk, with what would resolve it
quiz.why: Unknowns are risks until evidence says otherwise.

lessons.prompt:
I'm working through "Assess Technical Feasibility" (Discover → Feasibility & the Technical Decision) on my own project. Act as my assistant: draft and check, I decide.

Goal: Say, with evidence, whether each option can be built and run here — and on what conditions.
Done looks like: A feasibility assessment per option: rating, unknowns and how they were resolved, quality attributes at risk, skills and conditions.

I'll attach or paste: Architecture options; Spike results.

Work through these steps with me, one at a time:
1. Gather evidence & unknowns per option → Feasibility assessment
   For each architecture option, collect the spike results that support it and the unknowns that remain.
2. Rate each option → Feasibility assessment
   Rate each option's feasibility high / medium / low, citing the evidence, and name the quality attributes at risk.
3. Write skills & conditions → Feasibility assessment
   List the skills and capacity each option needs versus what the team has, and write each rating's conditions as checkable, dated facts.
4. Feasible? (a decision — give me the options and a recommendation; I make the call)
   Prepare the feasibility call for the tech lead: which options are feasible, and on what conditions.

Produce: Feasibility assessment. Use clear headings I can paste into my document.

Before you finish, check it against: Every rating cites spike results or docs; Conditions are specific and checkable; Evidence per rating; Checkable conditions.

Ask me for anything you need instead of guessing. Keep it specific to my project.

lessons.title: Estimate Effort, Risk & Cost
lessons.summary: Estimate each option as ranges, and log its risks with owners.

definition.purpose: Give each feasible option an honest effort range, run cost and risk picture, so the choice includes what it costs.
definition.outcome: An effort estimate as ranges per option and a risk register with likelihood, impact, owner and mitigation.
definition.jtbd: Help me say how big each option is and what could go wrong, without false precision.
exit: Every estimate a low / likely / high range with its basis
Every risk has an owner and a mitigation

normal: Break each option into work items
Estimate each as a three-point range
parallel: Estimating and risk-finding run in parallel

cases.happyPath: Ranges are reasonably tight and the top risks have mitigations.
alternates: Very uncertain item → wide range, plus a spike to narrow it
edgeCases: Reference data from past projects → use it to check the range
exceptions: Risk owned outside the team → named owner on the client side
failures: An option can't be estimated at all

routing.forward: Estimates & risk register → 1.5.3 Compare Options & Recommend
routing.alternate: Small option → one range and a short risk list
routing.escalation: Risk above the tech lead's appetite → client
routing.stop: Every option too big → back to framing or scope down — recorded in the learning log

criteria: Ranges with a basis, never single numbers
Every risk: likelihood, impact, owner, mitigation
policies: Risks above appetite are escalated, never hidden

decisions: How big, and how risky, is each option?

agents: AI coding agent for breaking down work
execution.authority: Tech lead accepts the estimates; risks above appetite go to the client.

continuity.handoff: Effort estimate & risk register → 1.5.3 Compare Options & Recommend
traceability: Creates EST-## and RSK-## linked to ARO-##

workflows.title: Estimate the Options
workflows.summary: Break each feasible option into work, estimate it as low / likely / high with its basis, add run cost, and log the risks a pre-mortem finds.

steps.title: Break each option into work items
steps.ask: Break each feasible option into work items small enough to picture — integration, logic, UI, tests, deployment, monitoring.

lenses.note: Work items small enough to estimate.

steps.title: Estimate three-point ranges & run cost
steps.ask: Estimate each item as low / likely / high days with its basis, add monthly run and support cost, and flag the widest ranges.

steps.title: Pre-mortem & rate the risks
steps.ask: Run a pre-mortem: 'it's six months later and this failed — why?' Turn the answers into risk-register rows with likelihood, impact, owner and mitigation.

steps.title: Within appetite?
steps.ask: Summarise effort, run cost and top risks per option for the tech lead, and flag anything beyond normal appetite.

lenses.note: Is effort and risk within the tech lead's appetite?

contract.definition: Break each feasible option into work, estimate it as low / likely / high with its basis, add run cost, and log the risks a pre-mortem finds.
decisions: Are effort and risk within appetite?
contract.handoff: Effort estimate & risk register → 1.5.3 Compare Options & Recommend
traceability: EST-## and RSK-## link to ARO-##
learning: Estimates vs actuals, checked in BUILD — learning log

objectives: Run a pre-mortem and own every risk
lessons.exercise: Estimate three work items for option A as low / likely / high with a basis, and add two risks with owners. Then do the same for your own project.

quiz.q: A risk has no owner. What happens?
options: Name an owner or escalate it
quiz.why: An unowned risk is a risk nobody manages.

lessons.title: Compare Options & Recommend
lessons.summary: Put the options side by side on the same evidence and make a clear recommendation.

definition.purpose: Make one clear, evidence-backed recommendation the tech lead can accept or challenge.
definition.outcome: An option comparison: each option against the targets, feasibility, effort, run cost and risk — and a recommendation with its trade-offs.
definition.jtbd: Help me recommend one approach and explain exactly why, including what we give up.
exit: Recommendation names what it trades away
Accepted or challenged by the tech lead

normal: Put the options side by side
Compare against targets, feasibility, effort, run cost and risk
parallel: Comparison drafted while trade-offs are discussed

cases.happyPath: One option is clearly best and the trade-offs are acceptable.
alternates: Close call → recommend the cheaper-to-reverse option
edgeCases: Recommendation depends on a condition → make it conditional
exceptions: Tech lead prefers another option → record the disagreement and the reason

routing.alternate: Single option → compare it with doing nothing
routing.escalation: Trade-off affects the client's targets → client
routing.stop: No acceptable option → stop and record why — recorded in the learning log

criteria: Every option compared on the same criteria
Recommendation is reversible or says why not
rules: Recommend, don't advocate — show the losing options fairly

decisions: Which approach, and what do we give up?

agents: AI coding agent for challenging the recommendation
execution.authority: Tech lead accepts or challenges the recommendation; the client decides trade-offs on their targets.

continuity.handoff: Option comparison & recommendation → 1.5.4 Record the Decision (ADR)
traceability: Recommendation links ARO-##, EST-## and RSK-##

workflows.title: Compare & Recommend
workflows.summary: Compare the options on the same evidence — targets, feasibility, effort, run cost, risk — name the trade-offs and recommend one.

steps.title: Put the options side by side
steps.ask: Put the options side by side on the same rows: quality targets met, feasibility, effort range, run cost, top risk, reversibility.

steps.title: Name the trade-offs
steps.ask: For each option, write what choosing it gives up compared with the others.

steps.title: Write the recommendation
steps.ask: Write the recommendation: one option, why, what it trades away, how reversible it is, and the conditions it depends on.

steps.title: Recommendation accepted?
steps.ask: Argue against my recommendation as a sceptical tech lead would, so I can strengthen it or change it.

lenses.note: Would you defend this recommendation in review?

contract.definition: Compare the options on the same evidence — targets, feasibility, effort, run cost, risk — name the trade-offs and recommend one.
decisions: Does the tech lead accept the recommendation?
recovery: Compare every option on the same rows
Add a 'what we give up' line
contract.handoff: Option comparison & recommendation → 1.5.4 Record the Decision (ADR)
traceability: Recommendation links ARO-##, EST-## and RSK-##

objectives: Compare options on the same rows
lessons.exercise: Write the 'what we give up' line for recommending option A. Then do the same for your own project.

quiz.q: Two options are close. Which do you recommend?
options: The one that's cheaper to reverse, with the reason
quiz.why: When the evidence is close, keep your options open.

lessons.title: Record the Decision (ADR) → Hand off to Plan
lessons.summary: Record the technical decision as an ADR and hand the evidence on to PLAN.

definition.purpose: Commit to an approach explicitly and leave a record anyone can follow later.
definition.outcome: A technical decision record (ADR) — context, decision, options considered, consequences — and the handoff pack for PLAN.
definition.jtbd: Help me record what we decided and why, so nobody has to rediscover it.
exit: ADR accepted by the tech lead

parallel: Learning captured while the pack is assembled

cases.happyPath: The ADR is accepted and PLAN takes the pack.
alternates: Decision is conditional → conditions and a date in the ADR
edgeCases: Not feasible → the ADR records 'do not build' and why
exceptions: Tech lead overrules the recommendation → the ADR records both

routing.forward: ADR & handoff pack → PLAN (Act II); learning → EVOLVE
routing.alternate: Small change → short ADR, same sections
routing.escalation: Decision beyond the tech lead → client
routing.stop: Not feasible → ADR says so; learning logged

criteria: Context, decision, options and consequences all present
rules: Every outcome is recorded — including 'do not build'
policies: ADRs are versioned, never edited silently

decisions: What do we build, and why?

execution.authority: Tech lead owns the decision; the client decides anything above the tech lead's authority.

continuity.handoff: ADR & handoff pack → PLAN; learning log → EVOLVE
traceability: Creates ADR-### and LRN-### linking TPS-##, ARO-##, EST-## and RSK-##

workflows.title: Record the Decision
workflows.summary: Record the decision as an ADR — context, decision, options, consequences — get it accepted, hand the evidence to PLAN and capture what discovery taught.

steps.title: Write the ADR
steps.ask: Write ADR-001 from my comparison: title, status, context, decision, options considered (each with why it lost), consequences (good and bad) and conditions.

steps.title: Link the evidence
steps.ask: Link every claim in the ADR to its evidence — spike, estimate, risk, baseline — and list anything unlinked.

lenses.note: Every claim links to a spike, estimate or risk.

steps.title: Decision accepted?
steps.ask: Prepare the decision review: the ADR summary and the questions the tech lead is likely to ask.

lenses.note: Security conditions carried in the ADR.

steps.title: Assemble the handoff pack
steps.ask: Assemble the handoff pack for PLAN: one paragraph per part (ADR, problem statement, options, estimates, risks, system context, metrics) with links.

lenses.note: Run and support needs in the pack.

steps.title: Capture what discovery taught
steps.ask: Write the learning-log entries from this discovery: what surprised us, what we'd do differently, and the change we'll make next time — each with an owner.

lenses.note: What would we do differently next time?

contract.definition: Record the decision as an ADR — context, decision, options, consequences — get it accepted, hand the evidence to PLAN and capture what discovery taught.
decisions: Does the tech lead accept the decision?
recovery: Write it up from the meeting the same day
Add the losing options and why they lost
contract.handoff: ADR & technical discovery handoff pack → PLAN (Act II); learning log → EVOLVE
traceability: ADR-### links TPS-##, ARO-##, EST-## and RSK-##

objectives: Write an ADR with context, options and consequences
Hand the evidence on to PLAN and capture learning
lessons.exercise: Write ADR-001 for the order-intake case. Then do the same for your own project.

quiz.q: The decision was 'do not build'. Is an ADR still needed?
options: Yes — it saves the next team from rediscovering it
quiz.why: Every outcome is recorded, including no.
